speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a rash on your scalp and forehead; to help me understand the cause, please describe how long you have had these symptoms and if you have noticed any blisters, scaling, or hair loss.

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap) with family history of psoriasis, though the "cold weather" exacerbation and scaling are consistent with both seborrheic dermatitis and early-onset psoriasis; the chronicity and distribution in an infant strongly favor seborrheic dermatitis. No further questions or tests are required for this clinical picture.
